The same rule as [verdict / duress_differ](verdict-duress-differ.md), under its `pin`-category name —
and the **same animation**, frame for frame. `PinDiffer` subclasses `DuressDiffer`
(`screens/pin/pin_differ.py:21`) and adds nothing: black hold, pill and dots arriving together
on the entrance law, the scanline across and back, the shake, the verdict beat, the caption. Every
timing, curve and constant lives on the twin; read its timeline there.

Both draw the same art, `pq1.procedural.pin_pill` (`pq1/procedural/pin_pill.py:33`), in the
warning orange #F5A033.

## Do / Don't

- **Do** retune the pace in `screens/verdict/duress_differ.py` only — this screen inherits it.
- **Don't** give this screen a timeline of its own again. One rule, one animation: two different
  pill films for the same refusal read as two different events.

## Port notes

- **Time is milliseconds, never frames.** Every animation here is a pure function of elapsed ms; the panel samples it at 14 fps. Do not count frames on the device — keep the ms clock and let the frame rate fall where it falls.
- The numbers on this page are read from the running Python at build time. If the page and the code ever disagree, the code wins — then run `python3 -m tools.handoff --check`.
- No one-shot accent is shorter than `VERDICT_ACCENT_MIN_MS` 145 ms (2.0 f) — two panel frames — or the panel may never show it.
